posts.title: The autumn sea bream are in
posts.excerpt: The whole-fish class moves to sea bream for October and November.
posts.content:
The fishmonger at Ōmichō brought the first autumn tai on Tuesday. They are firm, bright and the right size for a first whole fish.

From this week the whole-fish class works on sea bream: scaling, three pieces, sashimi from one side and the head simmered sweet.

posts.title: A new whetstone bench
posts.excerpt: Eight new stones and a long sink so the whole class can sharpen at once.
posts.content:
Aya’s father built a cedar bench along the back wall with a running-water trough. Eight stones sit on it now, one per counter.

Every class now ends with five minutes on the stone.

posts.title: Ichiban dashi at home
posts.excerpt: The stock we make in every class: kombu, katsuobushi and ten minutes.
posts.content:
Soak 10 g of kombu in a litre of water for an hour. Warm it slowly and lift the kombu out just before the water simmers.

Add 20 g of katsuobushi, turn off the heat, wait two minutes and strain without pressing. That is ichiban dashi.

posts.title: Packing a bento that travels
posts.excerpt: Cool everything first, pack the rice tight and keep wet things apart.
posts.content:
The bento class ends with packing: rice pressed firm in one corner, tamagoyaki standing on edge, the salmon on a shiso leaf.

Let everything cool before the lid goes on, and put the pickles in their own cup.
